**The Last Letter**

I found it tucked between the pages of an old book—yellowed, brittle, and smelling faintly of damp paper and something else, something like old ink and regret. The envelope was unmarked, but the handwriting inside was unmistakable.

*Dearest [Name],*

I don’t know how to say this without hurting you, but I have to go. Not forever—just for a while. The world is too much right now, and I need to be alone. I’ll write again when I can, but until then, please don’t look for me. Don’t call. Don’t ask.

I love you more than anything, but sometimes love isn’t enough. Sometimes it’s just… too much.

*—[Name]*

I held it in my hands, the weight of it pressing down like a stone. The book had been sitting on my shelf for years, forgotten, but now it felt like a relic—something from a life I no longer recognized. I had known [Name] once, in another time, before everything changed.

I closed the book gently, the letter slipping back into its place. The world outside was loud and bright, but inside, I felt the quiet hum of something unspoken. A part of me had always known this letter existed, even if I hadn’t wanted to believe it.

Maybe love wasn’t just about the words we say. Maybe it was about the letters we don’t write.

And the books we keep.
